subject.title: Make adaptive refresh agent-aware on fresh installs

question: Should fresh installations default to Adaptive and receive a first-run prompt for recurring local process and session inspection, or should local activity scanning remain a separate settings opt-in?
rationale: The measured benefit is narrow, global p95 is unchanged, scanning has privacy and CPU costs, and prior merged work approved Adaptive and Agent Sessions only as opt-in behavior.

options.title: Separate scanning from cadence
options.body: Default fresh installations to menu-only Adaptive and enable local coding-activity inspection only through a distinct explicit settings opt-in.

options.title: Approve the current consent prompt
options.body: Keep the first-run consent flow and recurring scanner after packaged upgrade, privacy, and performance proof is supplied.

options.title: Retain the five-minute default
options.body: Leave fresh installations at five minutes and keep both Adaptive cadence and activity scanning opt-in.

recommendation.title: Separate scanning from cadence
recommendation.body: Default fresh installations to menu-only Adaptive and enable local coding-activity inspection only through a distinct explicit settings opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: They established the accepted Agent Sessions implementation and its default-off product and privacy boundary.
